note: Layer 1: 30 PPI questions based on VIA 24 Character Strengths. 60% Likert, 40% Multiple Choice. Universal framing for ages 6-99.

items.prompt: When I need to solve a money problem, I can usually come up with ideas that others haven't thought of.
You hear about a new way to save money that sounds interesting but unfamiliar. What do you do?
options: A Look it up right away and learn more about it
B Ask someone who might know about it
C Keep it in mind but don't actively research it
D Stick with what I already know

items.prompt: Before making a big money decision, I think through all the pros and cons carefully.
Someone offers to teach you about investing for free. What's your first reaction?
options: A Yes! I want to learn everything I can
B I'm interested but only if it's quick
C Maybe, if I have time
D I'd rather not - it sounds boring or complicated

items.prompt: Friends and family often ask me for advice about money because I see the bigger picture.
You need to have a tough conversation with someone about money (like asking for a raise or setting a boundary). What do you do?
options: A I go for it - tough conversations don't scare me
B I do it eventually, but I stress about it first
C I avoid it unless I absolutely have to
D I usually find a way to get out of it

items.prompt: When I set a financial goal, I stick with it even when it gets hard.
I'm honest about my financial situation, even when it's embarrassing.
When you think about working on your finances, how do you feel?
options: A Energized - I'm ready to tackle it
B Motivated but a little tired
C Drained before I even start
D I'd rather do literally anything else

items.prompt: My relationships with family or friends are one of the main reasons I want to get my money together.
A friend is struggling with money and you have a little extra. What do you do?
options: A Help them out without thinking twice
B Help, but make sure I'm not putting myself in a tough spot
C Offer advice or support instead of money
D I'd want to help, but I can't afford to

items.prompt: I'm good at reading people's emotions, especially when money is involved.
I work well with others when it comes to managing money or making financial decisions together.
You and a roommate split bills. They've been short on cash lately. What's your approach?
options: A Everyone pays their share - no exceptions
B I'd cover them this time, but expect them to pay me back
C I'd adjust how we split things to make it easier for them
D I'd feel taken advantage of and bring it up

items.prompt: When a group needs to make a money decision, I often step up and take charge.
Someone close to you made a financial mistake that affected you. How do you handle it?
options: A I let it go pretty quickly - mistakes happen
B It bothers me for a while, but I move on eventually
C I forgive but don't forget
D I have a hard time getting over it

items.prompt: My biggest financial priority right now is:
options: C Saving for a specific goal
D Learning to manage money better

items.prompt: I think about future consequences before spending money.
You see something you really want but didn't plan to buy. What happens next?
options: A I walk away - if it wasn't planned, I don't buy it
B I think about it for a day or two before deciding
C I buy it but feel guilty afterward
D I buy it without thinking twice

items.prompt: My knowledge of investing is:
options: B Basic - I understand the concepts
C Limited - I'm just starting to learn
D None - It seems too complicated

items.prompt: I regularly feel thankful for what I have, even when money is tight.
When you think about your financial future, what comes to mind?
options: A I believe things will work out and get better
C I'm not sure - it could go either way
D I'm pretty pessimistic about it

items.prompt: My biggest financial challenge is:
I feel like managing my money well is connected to a bigger purpose in my life.
You're trying to save money but feel stuck. What's your move?
options: A I brainstorm new ideas or try something creative
B I look for tips online or ask for advice
C I keep doing what I've been doing and hope it works
D I give up - nothing seems to work anyway

items.prompt: You've tried to budget before and failed. What happens next?
options: A I try again with a different approach
B I take a break and come back to it later
C I feel discouraged but eventually give it another shot
D I assume budgeting just isn't for me

items.prompt: I'm good at controlling my impulses when it comes to spending.
No matter how bad my money situation gets, I believe I can turn it around.
Someone pitches you an investment opportunity that sounds too good to be true. What do you do?
options: A Research it thoroughly before deciding
B Ask trusted people for their opinions
C Go with my gut feeling
D Jump in if it sounds exciting

items.prompt: When something good happens with your money (like getting paid or finding extra cash), what do you feel?
options: C It's nice but doesn't change much
D I immediately think about what I need to spend it on
